newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo pledges to boost farm credits.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo pledges to boost farm credits.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Wednesday that the government would provide nearly 57 billion pesos in farm credits in 1997, up 30 percent from 1996.

"We will increase the sources of financing for all farmers, and so it is that this year close to 57 billion pesos will be at your disposal, 30 percent more than last year," Zedillo told farmers during a ceremony outlining the government's agricultural production plan until 2000.
In addition, Zedillo said his government would set aside more than 13.5 billion pesos to promote basic grains sales through such programs as Procampo and Alianza para el Campo.

"We will reach these goals by plainly supporting farmers: in the first place, the support for Procampo in this year alone will be 7.593 billion pesos and cover 14 million hectares (34.6 million acres)." ((-- Debora Montesinos, Mexico City newsroom, *525 728-7913))
